essence: A city so thickly coated with signs that the visitor sees only emblems pointing to other things, records the names the city gives itself, and leaves without ever having seen the city beneath them.
textDetails: Approach: days of walking among trees and stones; the eye notices a thing only when it reads it as the sign of another thing: a print in the sand means a tiger has passed, a marsh announces a vein of water, the hibiscus flower means winter is over; everything else is mute and interchangeable, trees and stones being only what they are.
The streets are thick with signboards jutting out from the walls; what the eye meets are not things but images of things that stand for other things.
Trade emblems: pincers mark the tooth-drawer's house, a tankard the tavern, halberds the barracks, scales the grocer's.
Statues and shields depict lions, dolphins, towers and stars, signs that something (no one knows what) has that emblem as its sign.
Prohibition signs: no entering the alley with wagons, no urinating behind the kiosk, no fishing with a pole from the bridge.
Permission signs: watering zebras, playing bowls, burning the corpses of relatives.

Through the temple doors the statues of the gods are visible, each shown with its attribute (the cornucopia, the hourglass, the medusa) so worshippers can recognise them and direct their prayers correctly.
Buildings with no signboard or figure are identified by their form and their position in the city's order: the palace, the prison, the mint, the Pythagorean school, the brothel.
Wares on the vendors' stalls are valued only as signs: the embroidered headband means elegance, the gilded palanquin power, the volumes of Averroes learning, the ankle bracelet voluptuousness.

The gaze runs along the streets as if they were written pages; the city dictates what to think and makes you repeat its discourse, so the visitor only records the names by which it defines itself and all its parts.
Whatever the city really is beneath this thick coating of signs, whatever it holds or hides, the visitor departs without ever having discovered it.
Outside, the land stretches empty to the horizon and the sky opens with fast-moving clouds.
In the shapes that chance and wind give the clouds, the departing traveler is already picking out figures: a sailing ship, a hand, an elephant.
Not in the text: colours, materials, size, walls or gates; water inside the city is implied only by the bridge of the no-fishing sign.
visualConcept: Tamara is staged as a city that consists of nothing but its own signage: a compact oval knot of streets on a dusty plain where every building is deliberately mute (pale, fog-coloured, low-contrast blocks with no doors or windows, like blank paper; the only openings in the whole city are the three temple doors, because the gods must be seen), while everything that signifies is crisp, saturated and lit. Hundreds of gilt and vermilion emblems hang from black iron brackets into every street, many of them three-dimensional trade objects (pincers, tankard, crossed halberds, scales) so they read from any angle, while shields and small statues show lions, dolphins, towers and stars, three temple doorways glow around gods holding cornucopia, hourglass and medusa, and the market lane's wares (headband, gilded palanquin, books, ankle bracelet) shine like emblems on their stalls. The streets are laid out as seven parallel 'lines' crossed by short alleys, so from the default camera the city reads like a ruled manuscript page with the emblems running along it like words. Five buildings carry no sign at all and declare themselves by archetypal form and placement: a domed, colonnaded palace on the central axis, a windowless prison cube inside a ring wall, a squat mint with a tall chimney and a coin-round oculus, a Pythagorean school assembled from perfect solids (cube, triangular pediment, dodecahedron finial), and a narrow brothel stacked with small curtained balconies at the market's end. Around the city lies a ring of identical, desaturated trees and stones (one instanced model each, silent and interchangeable), in which only three things are lit as signs: a trail of tiger prints across a sand patch, a reedy marsh with a faint luminous vein of water running beneath it toward the city, and one red hibiscus. Beyond, the empty plain runs to the fog horizon under a wide sky of racing clouds that now and then gather into a sailing ship, a hand, an elephant. The base is an endless flat sand plain dissolving into haze with the city on a barely raised mound; the test of success is that the signs feel like the only solid thing in Tamara.
layout: Convention: +X east, -Z north, default camera on the south. Ground: flat sand plain to the fog horizon (fog opaque by radius 60), city on a 0.3-high mound at the origin. City footprint: oval about 22 x 16 units, long axis on X. Seven parallel east-west streets ('text lines', 1.1 wide, 2.2 apart, pale paving) crossed by short north-south alleys at irregular intervals; one 0.8-wide canal runs north-south just west of centre with a single humped bridge on the middle street. About 150 building blocks (footprints 0.8 to 1.8, heights 0.9 to 2.6) packed between streets, all one matte putty material without openings. Instanced signage: about 420 hanging emblems on 0.3-long brackets at heights 0.9 to 1.8, roughly half small 3D gilt trade objects (pincers, tankard, crossed halberds, scales, 0.2 to 0.3 in size) and half double-sided painted boards (0.22 x 0.16) with lion, dolphin, tower, star glyphs on vermilion or ink fields; about 40 shields mounted flat on facades; 4 statues 1.0 tall on plinths at crossings (lion, dolphin, tower, star). Three small pedimented temples on the north edge with open doors framing 0.6-tall gods holding cornucopia, hourglass and medusa head, lit from within. Rule placards: 3 prohibitions (vermilion ring and slash: wagon at an alley mouth, kiosk on the market lane, fishing pole on the bridge) and 3 permissions (verdigris ring: a stone trough where 2 tiny zebras drink, a bowls green with balls, a stepped pyre platform at the city edge with a breathing ember). Market lane: east half of the middle street, 12 stalls with oversized glowing wares. Unmarked buildings: palace (centre north, 4 x 3, dome top at y=4.2), prison (west end, 2.5 cube inside a 3.5-radius wall), mint (east end, squat, chimney to y=4.0), Pythagorean school (south-west, about 3.0 tall), brothel (east edge, narrow 3.2-tall tower). Wilderness ring from radius 13 to 24: about 140 identical trees (1.2 to 1.6 tall) and 220 identical stones; at radius 17 to 20 a line of 12 tiger prints, a 3 x 2 marsh with reeds and a glowing vein running 4 units underground toward the city, and one emissive hibiscus. Clouds: a layer at height 25 to 40; cloud figures form to the north, behind the city as seen from the default camera.
signatureMotion: 1) The reading gaze: a soft warm highlight travels along the streets line by line, left to right, then drops to the next street like an eye reading a page; emblems under it flare and swing a little harder, so the city is visibly being read, one full 'page' about every 40 s (a uniform read-head position fed to the instanced emblem material). 2) Every emblem sways on its bracket with its own phase in the dry wind, glinting; temple interiors flicker, the zebras dip to drink, the pyre ember breathes. 3) Clouds race across the sky, and every 20 to 30 s a cluster of cloud puffs eases into a point-sampled silhouette (sailing ship, then hand, then elephant), holds about 4 s and shreds apart: the habit of reading signs follows you out of the city.
interactionDescription: Every emblem, shield, statue, divine attribute and glowing ware peels off the city in reading order and rises into a slowly turning gilded cloud above the rooftops, like a coating lifted away. What remains below is no revealed 'true' Tamara, only blank, doorless volumes that go grey and soft-edged and take on the exact colour of the stones outside: mute and interchangeable, beneath its signs the city cannot be discovered. Toggle back and the signs settle onto their brackets street by street.
mood: Late morning, dry and windy: a hard, clear sun that makes gilt and vermilion sparkle and throws sharp bracket shadows across blank walls; a pale dust haze softening the plain; high, fast clouds racing across a wide sky that fades from dusty blue to parchment at the horizon. A bright, crowded, over-explained place surrounded by vast silence.
caption: After days among trees and stones that mean nothing, you enter Tamara and stop seeing things at all. Every wall holds out an emblem: pincers, tankard, halberds, scales; gods display their attributes so no prayer goes astray; even the wares stand for virtues. You read the streets like lines on a page and leave knowing every name the city calls itself, nothing of the city. Out on the empty plain, a cloud is already becoming a ship.
motto: Where everything stands for something, nothing stands for itself.
camera: Default: distance about 30 units, elevation about 38 degrees, looking north about 15 degrees off the street axis so the seven street-lines run almost left to right across the frame like lines of text while the hanging emblems are seen at a readable angle; city centred slightly below frame centre, leaving the upper third for the racing clouds and their figures. Optional intro: start 1.2 units high among the identical trees of the approach, drift past the tiger prints and the hibiscus, then rise into the default view.
